Where everybody goes

All 73 plays from the Positioning Trainer, showing what the nine defenders do. Black arrows are the fielders. The dashed red line is the ball, numbered in the order it travels.

Get it Cover it Back it up Cut it Fielder moves Ball

Double Plays

1

The 6-4-3 Turn

Runner on 1st · 0 out

  1. Ground ball to short. Everyone moves on contact.
  2. Feed to second — the second baseman straddles the bag.
  3. Force at second. Turn and fire to first.
  4. Two outs. Right field backed up the throw the whole way.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Break toward the first-base side to back up the throw to first — if it gets away, you are the last line of defense.

  • C
    CatcherBack it up

    Trail the batter-runner up the line toward first in case the throw goes past the first baseman.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Get to the bag, give a clear target with your chest, and stretch only after you see the throw.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Straddle second, take the feed, touch the bag, and clear the runner as you throw to first.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Stay home and cover third — if the turn breaks down, that runner will try to keep going.

  • SS
    ShortstopGet it

    Field it, work through the ball toward second, and deliver a firm chest-high feed the pivot man can turn.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break in behind second base in case the feed sails into the outfield.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Sprint in toward second — you are the deep backup on the feed to the bag.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Sprint hard toward the line behind first. Every throw to first is your responsibility if it gets past.

Bunts

2

Bunt Down with a Runner Aboard

Runner on 1st · 0 out

  1. Bunt is down. Corners crash, second baseman breaks to first.
  2. Pitcher calls it and fields the ball clean.
  3. Sure out at first. Do not chase the lead runner.
  4. One out, runner in scoring position — that is the trade you accept.
  • P
    PitcherGet it

    Break off the mound under control, call the ball loud if it is yours, and field it with two hands facing first.

  • C
    CatcherBack it up

    You see the whole field — call who takes it and which base the throw goes to. Loudest voice on the play.

  • 1B
    First baseBack it up

    Crash hard at the bunt. If the pitcher takes it, peel off — but you must arrive like you are fielding it.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    The instant the bunt shows, sprint to cover first. Nobody else is going to be there.

  • 3B
    Third baseGet it

    Crash the line. Take anything bunted hard down third, and get back if the pitcher fields it.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    Cover second base behind the runner — if he rounds too far, that is a free out.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Move in behind third in case a throw comes across the diamond and gets away.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Break in behind second base to back up any throw to the bag.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Sprint toward the first-base line — the throw to first is coming and you are behind it.

3

Bunt Down the Third-Base Line — Bases Empty

Bases empty · 0 out

  1. Bunt is down. Corners charge, and the vacated bases get filled behind them.
  2. Field it clean — the out at first is the only one available.
  3. Throw to first.
  4. One out — and the base the fielder abandoned was covered the whole time.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Anything bunted up the middle is yours. Come off the mound under control and call it loud so two players do not arrive at once.

  • C
    CatcherBack it up

    Anything dying right in front of the plate is yours — mask off, pounce on it. On everything else you are the traffic cop: call who takes it and where the throw goes.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Cover first — the throw is coming there and the bag cannot be empty when it arrives.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover first. When the first baseman crashes on the bunt, you are the only one who can be there.

  • 3B
    Third baseGet it

    Charge it hard, field it with two hands, and throw to first. On a bunt the ball is slow — your feet have to be fast.

  • SS
    ShortstopBack it up

    Come in toward the infield. You are too far away to help unless you start running now.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Come in toward the infield. You are too far away to help unless you start running now.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Come in toward the infield. You are too far away to help unless you start running now.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Break in behind first. Bunt throws are rushed, and rushed throws sail.

4

Bunt Down the First-Base Line — Bases Empty

Bases empty · 0 out

  1. Bunt is down. Corners charge, and the vacated bases get filled behind them.
  2. Field it clean — the out at first is the only one available.
  3. Throw to first.
  4. One out — and the base the fielder abandoned was covered the whole time.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Anything bunted up the middle is yours. Come off the mound under control and call it loud so two players do not arrive at once.

  • C
    CatcherBack it up

    Anything dying right in front of the plate is yours — mask off, pounce on it. On everything else you are the traffic cop: call who takes it and where the throw goes.

  • 1B
    First baseGet it

    Charge it hard, field it with two hands, and throw to first. On a bunt the ball is slow — your feet have to be fast.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover first. When the first baseman crashes on the bunt, you are the only one who can be there.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Cover third and hold it — bunts are when kids drift and give away free bases.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    Cover second and hold it — bunts are when kids drift and give away free bases.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Come in toward the infield. You are too far away to help unless you start running now.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Come in toward the infield. You are too far away to help unless you start running now.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Break in behind first. Bunt throws are rushed, and rushed throws sail.

5

Wheel Play — Runners on 1st and 2nd

Runners on 1st & 2nd · 0 out

  1. Bunt is down. The wheel turns — third baseman crashes, shortstop rotates to third.
  2. Third baseman fields it looking at third — the lead runner is the prize.
  3. Throw to third for the lead out — but only if it is clean.
  4. Lead runner erased. If it is not there, take the sure out at first — never force the wheel.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Anything up the middle is yours. Field it and check third first — if the lead out is not there, take the sure one at first.

  • C
    CatcherBack it up

    Anything dying in front of the plate is yours, and you run the whole play with your voice — call the base out loud before anybody picks the ball up.

  • 1B
    First baseBack it up

    Crash the line hard. On a wheel play both corners charge, and the bases behind you get filled by somebody else.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Sprint to cover first. Both corners are charging, so that bag is yours and nobody else is close.

  • 3B
    Third baseGet it

    Crash hard and field it facing third. You are the reason this play gets the lead runner instead of settling for one out.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    This is the wheel. As the third baseman crashes, you rotate behind him to third and give a target for the lead out.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break in behind third base. That is where the throw is going and a miss there scores a run.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Come in behind second base in case the play swings back to the middle.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Sprint in behind first — the fallback throw goes there and it will be rushed.

6

Squeeze Bunt — Runner on Third

Runner on 3rd · 1 out

  1. Runner breaks from third with the pitch. The bunt goes down.
  2. Charge it and get it bare-handed — there is no time to field it cleanly and stand up.
  3. Flip it home. Underhand, firm, chest high.
  4. Bang-bang at the plate. This play is decided by how fast you get to the ball, not how hard you throw.
  • P
    PitcherGet it

    Come off the mound the instant you see the bunt turn. Bare hand it if you must and flip it home — the runner left on the pitch, so you have no time.

  • C
    CatcherCover it

    Get out from behind the plate for anything you can reach, then get back and cover home. If the pitcher takes it, your only job is to be a target and hold on.

  • 1B
    First baseBack it up

    Crash hard. On a squeeze everybody charges — hesitation is what makes this play work for the offense.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover first. Both corners are gone and the batter-runner still has to be accounted for.

  • 3B
    Third baseGet it

    Crash the line. Take anything down the third-base side and throw home without straightening up.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    Cover second and stay alert — if the throw home gets away, the batter-runner is going to keep running.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break in hard. If a throw home gets away, you are the reason it does not become two runs.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Come in toward second and stay ready for a wild scramble.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Sprint in behind first base for the throw that may come there instead.

Cutoffs & Relays

7

Base Hit to Left, Runner Trying to Score

Runner on 2nd · 1 out

  1. Line drive lands in left. The runner is going on contact.
  2. Left fielder charges through the ball. Third baseman lines up as the cutoff.
  3. Throw through the cutoff man, chest high.
  4. Cut or let it through — the catcher makes the call.
  5. Play at the plate — and the batter-runner stopped at first because the throw went home.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Get behind the plate, in line with the throw, and stay in foul ground. If it gets past the catcher you are the reason the runner behind him does not score too.

  • C
    CatcherGet it

    Guard the plate, give the fielder a target, and make the call — "cut home" or "let it go" — loud enough for the cutoff man to hear.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Cover first — the batter-runner is rounding and will take second if you leave the bag empty.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover second base. That batter-runner is the tying or winning run later; do not give him a free base.

  • 3B
    Third baseCut it

    You are the cutoff on the throw home. Line up between the left fielder and the plate, hands up, and be a loud target — cut it or let it through, but never guess.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    Cover third behind the runner in case he holds up or the play comes back to the bag.

  • LF
    Left fieldGet it

    Charge through the ball, field it on your throwing-hand side, and throw low through the cutoff man — never rainbow it home.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Sprint over and back up the left fielder. If he bobbles it, you are the reason it does not become a triple.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Drift in behind second base — every throw across the infield needs somebody behind it.

8

Base Hit to CF — Runner on 2nd Trying to Score

Runner on 2nd · 1 out

  1. Ball drops in. The runner was moving on contact.
  2. Field it and throw low through the cutoff man — never over his head.
  3. Catcher calls it. Cut and hold, or let it through for the tag.
  4. Play at the plate — and the batter-runner stopped at first because the ball went home.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Get behind the plate. On a throw home from the outfield, you are the one who keeps a second run from scoring.

  • C
    CatcherGet it

    Guard the plate, give a big target, and make the loudest call on the field — "cut home" or "let it go." The cutoff man cannot read your mind.

  • 1B
    First baseCut it

    You are the cutoff on a throw home from this side. Get out in a straight line between the center fielder and the plate, hands high, and be a target.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover first behind the cutoff man — the batter-runner will take second the second he sees the throw go home.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Cover third. If the runner holds up or the throw is cut, that is where the play goes next.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    Cover second base. That batter-runner is the run that beats you two innings from now.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break toward the ball and back up the center fielder. Two outfielders on every ball, always.

  • CF
    Center fieldGet it

    Charge through it, catch it moving toward the infield, and throw low through the cutoff. From center you have the straightest line home on the field.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Break over and back up the center fielder.

9

Base Hit to RF — Runner on 2nd Trying to Score

Runner on 2nd · 1 out

  1. Ball drops in. The runner was moving on contact.
  2. Field it and throw low through the cutoff man — never over his head.
  3. Catcher calls it. Cut and hold, or let it through for the tag.
  4. Play at the plate — and the batter-runner stopped at first because the ball went home.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Get behind the plate. On a throw home from the outfield, you are the one who keeps a second run from scoring.

  • C
    CatcherGet it

    Guard the plate, give a big target, and make the loudest call on the field — "cut home" or "let it go." The cutoff man cannot read your mind.

  • 1B
    First baseCut it

    You are the cutoff on a throw home from this side. Get out in a straight line between the right fielder and the plate, hands high, and be a target.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover first behind the cutoff man — the batter-runner will take second the second he sees the throw go home.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Cover third. If the runner holds up or the throw is cut, that is where the play goes next.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    Cover second base. That batter-runner is the run that beats you two innings from now.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break toward the ball and back up the play. Two outfielders on every ball, always.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Sprint over and back up the right fielder — you are 30 feet behind him on every ball to that gap.

  • RF
    Right fieldGet it

    Field it clean and throw low through the cutoff. Right field has the longest throw home, which is exactly why you never try to make it in the air.

Steals & Coverage

10

Who Covers on a Steal (Righty Hitting)

Runner on 1st · 1 out

  1. Runner breaks with the pitch.
  2. Catcher receives, steps, and throws — second baseman is covering.
  3. Tag applied in front of the bag, low and quick.
  4. Center field was sprinting in the whole time — that is why an overthrow costs one base, not two.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Get off the mound toward third — if the throw sails, you keep the runner from taking the extra base.

  • C
    CatcherGet it

    Receive, step toward second, and throw a strike to the bag — quick feet beat a big arm here.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Cover first — the throw is coming there and the bag cannot be empty when it arrives.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    With a right-handed hitter up, the bag is yours. Get there early, straddle it, and catch the ball before you look for the tag.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Hold your ground at third. Never leave that bag open on a steal of second.

  • SS
    ShortstopBack it up

    Stay on your side to field a ball hit to the left side — but be ready to back up the bag if the throw goes wide.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break in toward second on the throw — you are the backup on the left-field side.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Sprint straight in behind second base. Every catcher throw to second is yours to back up.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Move in behind first in case the catcher back-picks or the runner retreats.

11

Steal of Second — Lefty Hitting

Runner on 1st · 1 out

  1. Runner breaks with the pitch.
  2. Catcher receives, steps, and throws to the covering man.
  3. Low tag, applied in front of the bag.
  4. Out — because the right man covered and the wrong man did not guess.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Get off the mound toward the base being stolen and back it up. An overthrow here is a run.

  • C
    CatcherGet it

    Receive it clean, get your feet turned, and throw a strike to the bag. Quick feet beat a strong arm on every steal.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Hold first and stay ready for a back-pick if the runner is careless coming back.

  • 2B
    Second baseBack it up

    Stay home and be ready to field. Somebody has to still cover the ground the covering man left.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Hold third — never leave it open on a steal of second.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    With a lefty up, second base is yours. Beat the runner there and catch it first — the tag is the easy part.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break in behind the bag. On a steal of third, you are the only backup that exists.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Sprint straight in behind second base. Every catcher throw to second is yours to back up.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Come in behind first in case the play swings back that way.

12

Steal of Third

Runner on 2nd · 1 out

  1. Runner breaks with the pitch.
  2. Catcher receives, steps, and throws to the covering man.
  3. Low tag, applied in front of the bag.
  4. Out — because the right man covered and the wrong man did not guess.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Get off the mound toward the base being stolen and back it up. An overthrow here is a run.

  • C

  • 1B

  • 2B

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Get to third the instant the runner breaks, straddle the bag, and apply a low tag as you catch it.

  • SS
    ShortstopBack it up

    Stay on your side and cover the ground the third baseman left when he took the bag.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break in behind the bag. On a steal of third, you are the only backup that exists.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Sprint straight in behind second base. Every catcher throw to second is yours to back up.

  • RF

Pop-ups & Priority

13

Infield Pop-Up — Who Calls It

Bases empty · 1 out

  1. Ball goes straight up over the infield. Everybody looks for it.
  2. Shortstop calls it — three times, loud. Everyone else clears out.
  3. Caught. The pitcher and catcher got out of the way, which is their job.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Get out of the way. Your only job is to clear the area and point at the ball — never fight an infielder for a pop-up.

  • C
    CatcherBack it up

    Rip the mask off, find it, and clear out once an infielder calls it. You take it only if nobody does.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Cover first — the throw is coming there and the bag cannot be empty when it arrives.

  • 2B
    Second baseBack it up

    You and the shortstop have priority over the pitcher and catcher. Call it early and loud, or listen for the shortstop.

  • 3B
    Third baseBack it up

    Drift toward the ball and back up the shortstop — then get back to your bag once it is caught.

  • SS
    ShortstopGet it

    You have priority on anything you can reach. Call it three times, camp under it, and catch it above your eyes.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Come in hard. If the infielders lose it in the sun, you are the one who saves it.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Charge in behind the middle infielders — an outfielder coming in has the easiest play on a shallow ball.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Break in behind the second baseman and be ready to take charge if he waves off.

14

Foul Pop-Up Near First

Bases empty · 1 out

  1. Ball goes up into foul ground. Everybody looks first, then moves.
  2. Call it three times, loud. The trailing fielder becomes his eyes on the fence.
  3. Caught in foul ground — because two players worked it, not one.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Clear out and point at the ball. Your only job on a pop-up is to not be in the way.

  • C
    CatcherBack it up

    Mask off, find it, and be the voice — call the fielder off the fence or the dugout. He cannot look up and look around at the same time.

  • 1B
    First baseGet it

    It is yours. Turn your back to the infield, find it over your shoulder, and catch it moving toward the fence — that is the easier direction.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover first — the throw is coming there and the bag cannot be empty when it arrives.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Get back to third.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    Cover second base.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break in toward the line. Foul pop-ups get dropped, and a dropped one with a runner on is a live ball.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Come in behind the infield and stay alert.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Break in toward the line and back up the play.

15

Foul Pop-Up Near Third

Bases empty · 1 out

  1. Ball goes up into foul ground. Everybody looks first, then moves.
  2. Call it three times, loud. The trailing fielder becomes his eyes on the fence.
  3. Caught in foul ground — because two players worked it, not one.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Clear out and point at the ball. Your only job on a pop-up is to not be in the way.

  • C
    CatcherBack it up

    Mask off, find it, and be the voice — call the fielder off the fence or the dugout. He cannot look up and look around at the same time.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Get back to first and let the third baseman have it.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover second and stay out of it.

  • 3B
    Third baseGet it

    It is yours. Get under it early and catch it moving toward the line — and listen for the catcher on the dugout.

  • SS
    ShortstopBack it up

    Trail the third baseman toward the line and talk him through it — he is looking up, not around.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break in toward the line. Foul pop-ups get dropped, and a dropped one with a runner on is a live ball.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Come in behind the infield and stay alert.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Break in toward the line and back up the play.

Rundowns

16

Caught Off Third — Running the Pickle

Runner on 3rd · 1 out

  1. Runner is hung up off third. Catcher has the ball and runs at him.
  2. Catcher sprints him hard back toward third — never toward home.
  3. One throw, ahead of the runner, to the third baseman on the bag.
  4. Tag. One throw, no circus — and the pitcher already filled in behind the plate.
  • P
    PitcherCover it

    The second the catcher leaves the plate, it is yours — sprint in and stand on it. A rundown with nobody at home is how a run scores on a play you already had won.

  • C
    CatcherGet it

    Run him hard back toward third. Ball up, no fakes, and make one firm throw before he reaches the bag.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Cover first and stay alert — a rundown is exactly when a batter-runner sneaks into second.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover second in case the runner slips past and the play swings back around the diamond.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Hold the bag and give a target. Take the throw and apply the tag as the runner arrives.

  • SS
    ShortstopBack it up

    Slide in behind third base as the second man on that end. Rundowns need a body behind each bag.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Sprint in behind third. If a throw gets away over there, you keep the run from scoring.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Move in toward second and stay ready — rundowns turn into chaos, and chaos needs backup.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Break in behind first base and stay in the play until it is completely over.

17

Rundown Between First and Second

Runner caught between bases · 1 out

  1. Runner is hung up. The nearest fielder takes the ball and runs at him.
  2. Run him hard back toward the base he came from. Full speed, ball up.
  3. One throw, ahead of the runner, to the man on the bag.
  4. Tag. One throw, no circus — and every base still had somebody standing on it.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Fill in behind one end of the rundown. Rundowns fall apart when a base ends up empty — you are the spare body.

  • C
    CatcherCover it

    Stay home and protect the plate. Never leave it during a rundown; that is exactly when a second runner breaks.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Hold the bag and give a target. Take the throw and apply the tag as the runner comes back to you.

  • 2B
    Second baseGet it

    Take the ball and run at him hard toward first. Ball up, no pump fakes, one throw when he commits.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Hold third and give a target if the play comes back.

  • SS
    ShortstopBack it up

    Slide in behind the rundown as the extra man.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break in behind the play. If a rundown throw sails, you are the difference between one base and a run.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Sprint in behind second base. Rundowns produce more bad throws than any other play in youth baseball.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Come in behind first base and stay in it until the ball is dead.

  2. Run him hard back toward the base he came from. Full speed, ball up.

  4. Tag. One throw, no circus — and every base still had somebody standing on it.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover second and be ready to receive.

  • 3B
    Third baseGet it

    Take the ball and sprint him back toward second. Run him, do not dance with him — one firm throw ends it.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    Get to second and give a target. Catch it and tag — the runner is coming right back at you.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

First & Third

19

Corners Occupied — Hold the Ball

Runners on 1st & 3rd · 1 out

  1. Runner on first breaks with the pitch. The runner on third shortens up, waiting for you to throw.
  2. Catcher comes up throwing-ready — and looks the runner on third back.
  3. Hold it. No throw. The runner on third has to go back.
  4. They got second base. You kept the run off the board. That is a trade you take every time.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Stay in front of the mound as an outlet. If your catcher wants to hand it off or snap one to third, you are the middle man — but nobody is throwing to second here.

  • C
    CatcherGet it

    Catch it, come up ready, and look the runner on third all the way back. Then hold the ball. Throwing to second is exactly what the offense wants — a base is cheap, a run is not.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Cover first in case the runner stops halfway and tries to get back.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover second and give a target — but expect no throw. Your job is to be there if the catcher sees something free.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Stay on your bag with a target up. The runner at third is the entire reason this play exists — he is your responsibility.

  • SS
    ShortstopBack it up

    Back up second behind the second baseman and keep your eyes on the runner at third, not the one sliding in.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break in behind third. If anything is thrown over there, you are what stops a run.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Move in behind second base in case a throw does go through.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Come in behind first in case the runner breaks back that way.

20

Corners Occupied — The Cut Play

Runners on 1st & 3rd · 1 out

  1. Runner on first breaks. The shortstop cuts in front of second instead of covering it.
  2. Catcher throws to the cut man — short of the bag, chest high.
  3. The cut man reads the runner at third. He broke — so the ball goes home, not to the tag.
  4. Out at the plate. The cut is what gives you that choice — a throw to the bag would have been too late.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Cut toward the plate side and back up your catcher. This play can come home in a hurry.

  • C
    CatcherGet it

    Look him back first. If you throw, aim for the cut man in front of the bag — never all the way to second, because that throw cannot be brought back.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Hold first, then drift toward the plate side to help if the runner on third goes.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover second behind the cut. If the cut man lets it through, the tag is yours.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Stay on your bag. Chase nothing; your runner is the whole game right now.

  • SS
    ShortstopGet it

    You are the cut man. Break in front of the bag, catch it, and read third immediately — throw home if he broke, turn and tag if he did not.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Break in behind third in case the play swings back across the diamond.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Sprint in behind second — if the cut is missed, the ball is coming your way.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Come in behind first in case the catcher back-picks the runner returning.

Extra-Base Hits

21

Ball in the Gap to LF — Bases empty

Bases empty · 0 out

  1. Ball splits the gap. Two relay men go out, everybody else fills a base.
  2. Outfielder hits the relay man in the chest — the relay is why you never throw 250 feet.
  3. Relay turns and fires to third.
  4. Ball beat the runner because it took the short way home — two throws, not one hero throw.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Get behind third base. That is where this play is heading and where an overthrow would hurt most.

  • C
    CatcherCover it

    Guard the plate and run the whole play with your voice. You can see everything; nobody else can.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Cover first — the throw is coming there and the bag cannot be empty when it arrives.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Get to second and stand on it. The batter-runner is coming there, and an empty bag hands him the base — take the throw if the relay comes back your way.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Get to third and stay there. On a ball in the gap the runner is coming, and an empty bag is a free base.

  • SS
    ShortstopGet it

    You are the lead relay. Sprint out, get in a straight line between the left fielder and third, wave your arms, and be a loud target. Catch it, turn glove side, and throw.

  • LF
    Left fieldGet it

    This ball is yours — take the straightest line to it, get there under control, and come up throwing to the relay man. Do not drift; a gap ball punishes slow feet.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Sprint to back up the left fielder — get behind him, not beside him. If it skips past, you are the only thing between that ball and the fence.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Stay deep and get behind second, in line with the throw. If the relay sails past the bag you are the only thing between it and the fence.

Runner on Third

29

Ground Ball with a Runner on Third

Runner on 3rd · 1 out

  1. Ground ball to short. The runner at third bluffs to see if you panic.
  2. Look him back — eyes on the runner, feet under you. That freeze is the whole play.
  3. Now throw to first and bank the out.
  4. One out, and the runner never left. Chasing him is how you end up with nothing.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Get to a spot between the mound and the plate and read it. If the runner breaks for home, you are the backup plan.

  • C
    CatcherCover it

    Stay home and guard the plate. Tell the fielder what you see — "he is going" or "he is holding" — before he ever picks up his head.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Get to the bag and give a target. The out at first is the whole point of this play.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover second in case the throw pulls somebody off and the batter-runner tries to keep going.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Get back to third the moment the ball goes past you. If the runner retreats, that bag needs a body on it.

  • SS
    ShortstopGet it

    Field it, come up, and look the runner back at third first. Then throw to first. Do not rush your feet — you have time you do not think you have.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Come in behind the shortstop. On a ball hit right at somebody, the backup is the only thing that matters if it kicks.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Break in behind second base and stay alert — this play can turn into a rundown in a heartbeat.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Sprint in behind first. The throw is coming your way and rushed infielders sail throws.

30

Bases Loaded — Force at the Plate

Bases loaded · 0 out

  1. Ground ball to short with the infield in. Every runner takes off — all four are forced.
  2. Throw home. The run is the out you want — take it first.
  3. Force at the plate. Catcher steps inside the line and looks to first.
  4. Two outs, no run. That is the best possible outcome of a bases-loaded ground ball.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Back up the plate. With the bases loaded, a throw that gets past the catcher can score two, not one.

  • C
    CatcherCover it

    Keep your foot on the plate for the force, catch it clean, then step to the inside of the line and throw to first. Force first, tag never.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Cover first — the throw is coming there and the bag cannot be empty when it arrives.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover second. If the ball is hit to your side, the force there is your play instead.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Hold third for the force. Every base is a force with the bases loaded, so nobody needs to tag anybody.

  • SS
    ShortstopGet it

    Field it and check your feet — with the infield in, the throw home is short and easy. Give the catcher something chest high he can handle.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Come in behind the shortstop. With everybody running, a booted ball costs runs immediately.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Break in behind second and be loud — you can see the whole infield from behind them.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Sprint in behind first for the second half of the double play.

Loose Balls

35

Ball Gets Away with a Runner on Third

Runner on 3rd · 1 out

  1. Ball skips past the catcher. The runner breaks for home immediately.
  2. Catcher finds it fast; pitcher is already covering the plate.
  3. Flip it — underhand, firm, chest high. No fancy throws from your knees.
  4. Tag at the plate. This play is won by two players starting to run at the same instant.
  • P
    PitcherCover it

    Sprint to the plate the instant the ball hits the dirt. Straddle the front edge, give the catcher a target, and hold on. This is your out to make.

  • C
    CatcherGet it

36

Dropped Third Strike

Bases empty · 2 out

  1. Strike three in the dirt. The batter takes off — with two outs he can always run.
  2. Catcher finds it and steps to the INSIDE of the baseline — never throw through the runner.
  3. Throw to first to end the inning.
  4. Inning over — on a strikeout that was almost a baserunner.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Come off the mound toward the first-base line and back up the throw. This throw is rushed more often than any other.

    CatcherGet it

    Find the ball, then move to the inside of the baseline before you throw — a throw that hits the runner in the back is a free base.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Get to the bag fast and give a clear target. The catcher is throwing on the run and needs something obvious to aim at.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover second in case the throw gets away and the batter-runner keeps going.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Hold third. It is empty, and an empty base is exactly where a hustling runner ends up.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    Cover second with the second baseman and be ready for a play there if the ball gets loose.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Move in — you are far from this play, but if it goes wrong it goes very wrong.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Break in behind second base in case the throw sails into the outfield.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Sprint in behind first base. This is the single most overthrown play in youth baseball.

Pickoffs

37

Pickoff at First

Runner on 1st · 0 out

  1. Pitcher comes set. The runner leans just a little too far.
  2. Spin and throw — knee high, on the bag side.
  3. Low tag, straight down. The runner is diving back and the tag has to already be there.
  4. Out — and even here, right field was moving behind the bag the whole time.
  • P
    PitcherGet it

    Come set, hold long enough to make him relax, then make a quick accurate throw knee high to the bag side. Speed of feet beats speed of arm.

  • C
    CatcherBack it up

    Watch the lead and call it — you can see how far he is off better than anyone. If he leans, tell your pitcher.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Hold the runner on, take the throw, and apply a quick tag straight down at the corner of the bag. Catch it first, always.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover second — if the runner breaks the other way instead of diving back, that is where the play goes.

  • 3B
    Third baseCover it

    Stay at third. Never leave that bag unattended during a pickoff, no matter how exciting it looks.

  • SS
    ShortstopBack it up

    Cheat toward second and be ready for a rundown. Pickoffs turn into pickles more often than they turn into easy outs.

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

    Take a few steps in and stay awake — you are one bad throw from being in this play.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Move in behind second base in case this becomes a rundown.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Break in behind first base on every pickoff throw. If it gets past, you keep the runner out of scoring position.

40

Ground Ball to 3B — Bases empty

Bases empty · 0 out

  1. Ground ball to third. Everybody has a job before it is even fielded.
  2. Throw to first.
  3. Play made. Watch the backups: nobody ran across the diamond, everybody covered what was beside them.
  • P
    PitcherCover it

    Get to the plate and protect it. On a ball in the dirt or a wild throw, you are the last man home.

  • C
    CatcherBack it up

    Trail the batter-runner up the line and back up the throw to first. If it gets past the first baseman, you are why it costs one base instead of two.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Beat the runner to the bag, straddle it, and catch the ball before you think about the tag.

  • 3B
    Third baseGet it

  • SS
    ShortstopBack it up

  • LF
    Left fieldBack it up

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Sprint in and back up second base. You cover more ground than anybody — use it.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

Tag-Ups & Sac Flies

71

Fly Ball to LF — Runner on 3rd, Less Than Two Outs

Runner on 3rd · 1 out

  1. Ball in the air. The runner goes back and tags up.
  2. Caught — and the runner leaves the instant the ball touches the glove.
  3. Throw home through the cutoff man, chest high.
  4. Catcher makes the call — cut it, or let it through for the play at the plate.
  5. Play at the plate. This is the throw that decides one-run games.
  • P
    PitcherBack it up

    Get behind the plate. On a tag-up throw home, if it gets past the catcher the next runner scores too.

  • C
    CatcherGet it

    Set up at the plate, give the outfielder a target, and make the call on the cutoff — "cut home" or "let it go." Block the plate legally and hold on.

  • 1B
    First baseCover it

    Cover first — the batter is not a runner on a caught fly, but a missed catch changes everything.

  • 2B
    Second baseCover it

    Cover second base and watch for a trailing runner trying to advance while the throw goes home.

  • 3B
    Third baseCut it

    You are the cutoff on a throw home from left. Line up, hands up, and be loud — then get back to your bag if the catcher lets it through.

  • SS
    ShortstopCover it

    Cover second with the second baseman and be ready to take a cut throw if the play at the plate is dead.

  • LF
    Left fieldGet it

    Get behind the ball so you catch it moving toward the infield with your momentum going home. Catch it above your throwing shoulder, crow-hop, and throw low through the cutoff — a one-hop strike beats a rainbow every time.

  • CF
    Center fieldBack it up

    Break toward the ball and back up the left fielder. A dropped fly with a runner tagging is a disaster you can prevent by being 30 feet behind him.

  • RF
    Right fieldBack it up

    Break toward the ball and back up the left fielder. A dropped fly with a runner tagging is a disaster you can prevent by being 30 feet behind him.
